Theme

Money, work & business · Church life

collection noun

of money, for a common purpose

also take up a collection, whip-round, church collection, a collection for, chip in, contribution

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.233
Vulg. 1 Cor. 16.1

collēcta, collēctae f.

noun, first declension

a contribution of money, a collection

Each guest’s share of a dinner in Cicero; in the Vulgate the collection for the church at Jerusalem, and so the church collection. collēcta is also a gathering of people in Christian Latin (Jerome; Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • stips, stipis f. — a gift in small coin, alms, an offering

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 25.12: stipem Apollinī cōnferre (Lewis & Short); Cic. Leg. 2.40 (Lewis & Short)

    The small coins given to a god, a temple or a beggar; stipem cōnferre, to give to a collection. The nominative is not found.

Examples

  • quoniam conlēctam ā convīvā, Crasse, exigis, nōn committam ut, sī dēfūgerim, tibi causam aliquam recūsandī dem

    since you demand my share like a dinner guest’s, Crassus, I won’t back out and give you an excuse to refuse yoursCic. de Or. 2.233

  • Dē collēctīs autem, quae fīunt in sānctōs

    Now concerning the collection for the saintsVulg. 1 Cor. 16.1

See also money, church, give, pay.

SourcesLewis & Short: collecta · Lewis & Short: stips
